html:
A line of Roman frontier defences about 550 km long that cut across south-west Germany from the Rhine to the Danube, in use from about 83 to 260 CE.

After the Teutoburg Forest, Rome held the Rhine and Danube as its northern borders. The two rivers left an awkward angle of land between them. Starting with Domitian's war against the Chatti in 83 CE, Rome moved forward and closed the gap with a line of watchtowers and forts linked by a patrol road. Hadrian added a continuous wooden palisade. Later came a bank and ditch, and in Raetia a stone wall.

It was not built to stop an army. It marked the edge of Roman rule and let soldiers watch and control who crossed, and where they traded and paid duties.

During the Crisis of the Third Century, under pressure from the Alamanni, Rome gave it up around 260 CE and fell back to the rivers. Its remains, such as the rebuilt fort of Saalburg, are part of a World Heritage Site with Hadrian's Wall.
sum: A line of Roman frontier defences about 550 km long that cut across south-west Germany from the Rhine to the Danube, in use from about 83 to 260 CE.
